content.text: •begins in lungs, can disseminate; MC in resource-limited countries, rare in US
•LTBI PATHO: delayed-type hypersensitivity; T cells → cell-mediated immune response → caseating granulomas; dormant unless IS → bacteria multiply → active TB
•from an infected pt w/ active dz
•drug use (ex, homelessness, incarceration), tobacco & EToH abuse
•systemic dz (ex, silicosis, hematologic malig, CKD, celiac dz, cirrhosis, COPD)
•children <5yo, older adults, household contacts, travel to endemic area
•crowding/poor ventilation (ex, hospitals, nursing homes, homeless shelters, college dorms)
•high-risk health care settings (ex, urban coastal hsp, facilities serving ↓SES pts or many immigrants from high-risk countries)
•born in a TB-endemic area, organ transplant
RF for progression (latent → active): IS (ex, HIV, chemo, steroids, biologics), DM, kidney inj, malignancy
↑fever d/t TB PNA, pleurisy w/ effusion, lymphadenitis
•PE ⍉reliable → labs + CXR for any pt w/ suspicious pulm Sx
•Rasmussen aneurysm: pulm A. aneurysm that begins in a TB cavity + spreads to the bronchial arteries → rupture = massive hemoptysis
•Lifetime risk of reactivation = 10% w/ 5% w.in first 18mo
– placement: tuberculin injected just beneath the skin of the volar forearm (27-gauge, bevel up) → pale 1.0cm wheal
– read 48-72h → measure transverse diameter of induration (⍉erythema)
– ⍉gold strd for LTBI dx; PPD induration width vs pt's RFs → need for further testing (USU CXR)
– ≥5mm: HIV, recent TB contact, CXR c/w prior TB, organ transplant, TNF-alpha inhibitors, chronic steroids, other IS, clin evidence of TB dz

– ≥10mm: immigration from high-prevalence country <5yrs ago, IVDU, residents/employees of high-risk settings (shelters, correctional facilities, hospitals, nursing homes), mycobacteriology lab workers, comorbid (ex, DM, severe kidney dz, Hodgkin, lymphoma, malnutrition), <90% IBW, children <4yo or exposed to high-risk adults, children born in high-prevalence regions
•HIV: baseline PPD; annual testing if initial test ⊖ + ongoing RFs (communal living, active drug use, incarceration)
•IGRA (blood): preferred; specific for TB infect but can't distinguish latent vs active
– ⍉return visit to read; distinguishes ⊕TST d/t BCG or nontuberculous mycobacteria
•⊕screen → CXR + clin eval to determine latent vs active
– asx pt w/ 1 ⊕screen → confirm w/ IGRA; both ⊕ → eval for active TB (CXR, other imaging, sputum)
: hilar &/or mediastinal LAD, pleural effusion, segmental or lobar consolidation
– primary TB consolidation ⇢ middle &/or lower lobe
AFB smear = sufficient for DX in at-risk pts
•AFB cx of resp secretions = gold strd; sample via flexible bronchoscopy w/ bronchial washings
•AFB stain: less sensitive than cx but fast; cx growth can take up to 8wks
•tissue bx: granulomatous inflam w/ caseation necrosis
•meningitis, ocular, renal, pericarditis, salpingitis, peritonitis, intestinal
Alt (susceptible dz): 4mo INH + rifapentine + PZA + moxifloxacin
•monitor LFTs; add vit B6 (pyridoxine) → prevent periph neuropathy d/t INH
•MDR-TB: INH-monoresistance regimen, BPaLM, or BPaL based on resistance patterns
•exact regimen + monitoring (pt age, comorbidities) per ID specialists + local health dept
MDR-TB: FQ (ex, levofloxacin) = 2nd-line; linezolid = last-line (severe SE, poor long-term tolerance)
Inpt active TB: negative-pressure isolation room; clinicians wear N95
Prognosis: good w/ tx; MCC tx failure = ⍉taking meds
•fatal w/o tx; mortality ⇡ in resource-limited countries
